title: Rows Columns and Data Types
outcome: By the end, I can read a table schema and distinguish a numeric value from its text representation.
scenario: A fictional approved book catalogue has three fields per row.
given: Schema: id is nonempty text; pages is an integer 1–300; illustrated is Boolean True or False.

steps.label: Column contract
steps.detail: Field names identify values; order is not the only guide.

steps.label: Validate A
steps.detail: B7 is text, 90 is allowed integer, True is Boolean: valid.

steps.label: Validate B
steps.detail: Quoted "90" is text, so pages fails the integer contract.

steps.label: Validate C
steps.detail: Empty id fails even though its other two values have allowed types.

explanation: A schema makes row meanings and expected types explicit. The string "90" looks like a number when printed but does not meet this strict integer schema. A repair can be authorised later, but must not be assumed silently. Missing or empty identifiers also prevent tracing an item back to its source.

counterfactual.change: Change B’s pages from "90" to integer 90 using an approved repair.
counterfactual.prediction: B now satisfies the declared schema.
counterfactual.reason: Its id is nonempty and illustrated is Boolean; the page-type defect is removed.

student_task: Which two rows originally fail, and do they fail for the same reason?
teacher_answer: B fails pages type; C fails empty id. A passes all three field checks.
project_evidence: Publish the recommender’s row schema and validation results before ranking books, preserving repair provenance.
limits: Schema validity does not confirm that the book really has 90 pages or that its metadata is accurate.
review_note: Individually reviewed fictional topic example; arithmetic and declared policies checked. This is supported practice, not the reserved independent assessment.
